proposals.defect: placements() unions rendered_examples - every example the plan renders, in any section - into every destination's covered set, so any preserved unit anywhere that cites a rendered example's fact ID is dropped, including a unit whose relation to the example is evidentiary rather than introductory. Arrival item 65's own measured shape was adjacency (Cells-.NET's inherited_unit:018.paragraph immediately before inherited_unit:019.code_block); the rule as written is scoped by neither destination, position, nor unit kind.
proposals.proposed_shape: Scope rendered_examples to the inherited unit adjacent to that example's own code block in the source document - the example fact's evidence already names its unit ('unit inherited_unit:056.code_block') and every inherited unit carries its source line range, so adjacency is deterministic with no new input. A narrower variant that also closes the measured defect: exempt units of kind table or list, which no lead-in ever is. Mutation test: a preserved paragraph immediately before an example's code block still drops, a preserved table three units later citing the same example places, and the Cells-.NET line-155 shape still drops.

proposals.title: section_authoring's output is unbounded at every level, and a truncation aborts the run without storing what truncated

Under constrained decoding nothing terminates the generation - the shape F2 diagnosed at S4 and item 59 fixed at S5, in the only remaining job whose output array is unbounded at both levels. jobs.py then fails closed on finish_reason == 'length' and, because store.put runs only after a successful parse, writes no calls/<id>.rejected-N.json, so the text that overran is not in the transaction. proposals.alternative_rejected: Raising max_output_tokens - the option the error message lists first and the one an unbounded array defeats at any budget.
